Image Meet Luz Congresswoman Luz Rivas is an engineer, educator, and public servant who was elected to the House of Representatives in 2025 to represent California’s 29th Congressional District – the first Latina to represent the district and the only Latina in Congress with a STEM background.  For the 119th Congress, Rep. Rivas was elected by her peers to serve in House Democratic Leadership as the Freshman Leadership Representative. In this role, she ensures each freshman member’s voice is heard and represented in the House Democrats’ agenda, and participates in Democratic Leadership meetings. Additionally, Rep. Rivas is a member of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, Congressional Progressive Caucus, and the Democratic Women’s Caucus.  Prior to her election to the House of Representatives, Rep. Congresswoman Luz Rivas Introduces Bill to Strengthen Telecommunications Infrastructure During Natural Disasters | Representative Luz Rivas Skip to main content Congresswoman Luz Rivas Introduces Bill to Strengthen Telecommunications Infrastructure During Natural Disasters September 3, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Luz Rivas (CA-29) introduced the Telecommunications Gaps in Accountability and Performance (GAP) Act to ensure effective communications during natural disasters. During the Palisades, Eaton, and Hurst wildfires in January 2025, connectivity failures directly affected evacuations, emergency response coordination, and public safety communications. These disruptions emphasized the need for congressional oversight of existing disaster response frameworks, including the Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative (MDRI). The Telecommunications GAP Act requires the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to issue a report to Congress evaluating the effectiveness of the MDRI.    “During the January 2025 wildfires, families across Los Angeles experienced firsthand how quickly communications can fail when they need them most,” said Congresswoman Rivas. “When an evacuation order comes, people must be able to rely on their phones and wireless networks to get alerts, reach loved ones, and hear from first responders. My Telecommunications GAP Act ensures Congress has a clear, independent assessment of what worked during last year’s wildfires across L.A. County, as well an analysis to close any gaps in disaster communications systems to better protect people and their homes. A resilient and reliable telecommunications infrastructure is key to keeping our communities safe, especially as wildfires and climate-driven disasters become more intense.”   Background:    The Telecommunications Gaps in Accountability and Performance (GAP) Act  will require the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to issue a report to Congress evaluating the effectiveness of the Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative (MDRI), including  an analysis of the January 2025 Palisades, Eaton, and Hurst fires in Los Angeles.   The Federal Commu

Congresswoman Luz Rivas Introduces Bill to Protect Public Health and Our Environment, Holds Oil and Gas Accountable | Representative Luz Rivas Skip to main content Congresswoman Luz Rivas Introduces Bill to Protect Public Health and Our Environment, Holds Oil and Gas Accountable August 6, 2026 Press Release LOS ANGELES — Congresswoman Luz Rivas (CA-29), member of the House Committee on Natural Resources, introduced the Methane Pollution Accountability Act , a bill that holds oil and gas companies accountable for the harmful pollutants and toxins released into communities through venting, flaring, and leaking processes. These communities are often subjected to worse public health, with increased rates of disease such as asthma or cancer. “For far too long, oil and gas companies have treated environmental justice communities as a dumping ground at the expense of the health and well-being of the families who live there,” said Congresswoman Rivas. “In the San Fernando Valley, decades of harmful emission practices have led to higher rates of asthma, respiratory illnesses, organ damage, and other serious health conditions. My Methane Pollution Accountability Act holds oil and gas companies accountable for their harmful practices to minimize the pollutants being leaked into environmental justice communities like ours. It is my hope that House Republicans put our communities ahead of oil and gas interests and bring this bill to the floor.” “We are grateful for Representative Rivas’ leadership in holding big polluters accountable for the damage they continue to cause to our health and the environment,” said Madeleine Foote, Healthy Communities Program Director at League of Conservation Voters. “At a time when the Trump Administration caters to the fossil fuel industry and their profits rather than the health and safety of our families, it is more important than ever for Congress to step up and ensure we are prioritizing clean air for every community.” “Companies who refuse to adopt readily-available technology to reduce routine venting and flaring should absolutely have to have a plan in place to minimize pollution and leaks or pay for their waste,” said Mahyar Sorour, D

Congresswoman Luz Rivas Secures $850,000 in Federal Funding for Key Pacoima Wash Infrastructure and Safety Improvements | Representative Luz Rivas Skip to main content Congresswoman Luz Rivas Secures $850,000 in Federal Funding for Key Pacoima Wash Infrastructure and Safety Improvements August 13, 2026 Press Release LOS ANGELES — Congresswoman Luz Rivas (CA-29), representative for California’s 29th Congressional District, presented the City of Los Angeles with $850,000 in federal funding for the Pacoima Wash Bridge Mitigation Project. This funding will help improve the safety and security of six critical bridges that cross the Pacoima Wash. “I am proud to secure $850,000 in federal funding to make key safety improvements to six bridges that cross the Pacoima Wash,” said Congresswoman Rivas. “For decades, people have crossed the Pacoima Wash to get to work, go to school, and run errands. The funding I secured will make the necessary repairs and upgrades to reduce fire and safety hazards so people can continue safely crossing the Pacoima Wash for years to come. I will continue working with Councilwoman Imelda Padilla and our community partners to secure federal funding and resources that keep San Fernando Valley residents safe.”   “This investment will make a real difference by helping us address serious safety hazards, protect critical infrastructure and create safer conditions for residents, pedestrians and our unhoused neighbors. Public assets, like the Pacoima Wash bridge are essential, and this funding will allow us to reinforce and secure these areas while protecting them for years to come,” said Councilwoman Imelda Padilla. “This is what strong collaboration can deliver for our communities, and I am incredibly grateful to Congresswoman Luz Rivas for her continued partnership, leadership and commitment to bringing critical federal resources home to the East San Fernando Valley.”   Background: Congresswoman Rivas secured $850,000 in Fiscal Year 2026 Community Project Funding to improve the safety and security of six bridges that cross the Pacoima Wash. Congresswoman Luz Rivas on Bipartisan Housing Bill Becoming Law after Trump’s Refusal | Representative Luz Rivas Skip to main content Congresswoman Luz Rivas on Bipartisan Housing Bill Becoming Law after Trump’s Refusal July 11, 2026 Press Release LOS ANGELES — Congresswoman Luz Rivas (CA-29) release d the following statement after the 21 st Century ROAD to Housing Act became law. Trump previously refused to sign the bill into law after it overwhelmingly passed the House of Representatives because he continues to focus on disenfranchising millions of voters rather than help working Americans achieve homeownership.   “For over two weeks, Trump held our bipartisan housing bill hostage because he would rather make it harder to vote than make life more affordable for working families,” said Congresswoman Rivas . “We are in a housing crisis and Americans need help now. Too many constituents across the San Fernando Valley have told me the high costs of housing have put homeownership out of reach for them. Trump prolonged the delivery of much-needed housing relief because he believes the affordability crisis is a ‘hoax’. Trump would rather focus on restricting ballot box access for millions of Americans. I will continue working with House Democrats to make housing affordable for all, address the affordability crisis created by Trump and his Congressional Republicans, and stop Trump’s ongoing attempts to rig our elections.”   Background: On June 23, 2026, the House of Representatives passed the 21 st Century ROAD to Housing Act by a vote of 358-32. This bill was originally supposed to be signed into law on June 24, 2026, by President Trump in a signing ceremony on Capitol Hill. Congresswoman Luz Rivas, Supervisor Lindsey Horvath Meet with FAA to Advance Safety Improvements at Whiteman Airport | Representative Luz Rivas Skip to main content Congresswoman Luz Rivas, Supervisor Lindsey Horvath Meet with FAA to Advance Safety Improvements at Whiteman Airport July 13, 2026 Press Release LOS ANGELES — On Thursday, July 9, 2026, Congresswoman Luz Rivas (CA-29), representative for California’s 29 th Congressional District, and Los Angeles County Supervisor Lindsey P. Horvath met with officials from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to advocate for stronger safety measures and oversight at Whiteman Airport following two recent aircraft crashes involving aircraft landing at the airport in Pacoima.   The meeting follows Congresswoman Rivas’ and Supervisor Horvath continued advocacy after the April 20, 2026, and June 16, 2026, crashes. These efforts include Supervisor Horvath’s letters sent directly to FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford calling for a temporary suspension of flight operations pending comprehensive investigations into the recent incidents, enhanced oversight of pilot training and aircraft maintenance, a thorough review of airport operations, and immediate safety recommendations.   Los Angeles County has conducted an analysis of crashes that have occurred in the last 25 years and cross referenced them with National Traffic Safety Board (NTSB) investigations. According to the NTSB, every single crash has been caused by pilot error or aircraft malfunction.   “The meeting on Thursday with myself, Supervisor Horvath, and FAA was productive in ensuring safety and accountability at Whiteman Airport,” said  Congresswoman Luz Rivas.  “I look forward to seeing the FAA fulfill its commitments to increase inspections, community outreach, and education at Whiteman Airport. I have the highest standards and expectations for the FAA to ensure safety for those who use the airport as well as the continued safety for the surrounding community of Pacoima.”   “The safety of Pacoima residents will always be my top priority,” said Supervisor Lindsey P. Congresswoman Luz Rivas Conducts Oversight at Dilley Family Detention Facility in Texas, Raises Alarm Over ICE Secrecy | Representative Luz Rivas Skip to main content Congresswoman Luz Rivas Conducts Oversight at Dilley Family Detention Facility in Texas, Raises Alarm Over ICE Secrecy July 28, 2026 Press Release Dilley, Texas — Congresswoman Luz Rivas (CA-29), representative for California’s 29th Congressional District, conducted a Congressional oversight visit of the Dilley Immigration Processing Center in Texas with her colleagues, Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20), Congresswoman Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07), and Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07). The Members visited the Dilley Immigration Processing Center to meet with women, children, and families who have been detained for extended periods of time and conduct oversight on the conditions of the facility, which has been consistently reported as inhumane and dire. “My colleagues and I met with 20 people, including a 16-year-old, who have been detained at the Dilley Immigration Processing Center for months,” said Congresswoman Rivas. “I spoke with a woman from Maryland who was attending her court hearing in March when she was detained and sent to the Dilley Immigration Processing Center. Her 12-year-old son with special needs has a court hearing tomorrow and is worried that he, too, will be sent to the Dilley Immigration Processing Center or even deported. This is one story among hundreds – of mothers detained, children pulled away from school, families separated, and lives being disrupted in ways that often go unseen. We owe it to these families to listen and respond.”   Unfortunately, ICE officials on-site severely limited access to Members. More specifically, the Members were only able to talk to one child, even though over 100 children are detained. Members were not shown the medical unit nor classrooms, which were of particular importance especially to determine the conditions of the facility. Congresswoman Luz Rivas Statement on Massie Amendment to Republican State, Foreign Operations Appropriations Bill | Representative Luz Rivas Skip to main content Congresswoman Luz Rivas Statement on Massie Amendment to Republican State, Foreign Operations Appropriations Bill July 15, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Luz Rivas (CA-29) released the following statement on Republican Amendment #8 to the National Security, Department of State and Related Programs Appropriations Act:   “Foreign policy, especially issues involving the Middle East, should be considered by lawmakers in a thoughtful and strategic approach. Unfortunately, while I disagree with many of the actions of far-right Netanyahu, the Republican amendment is a poorly drafted and hyper-partisan amendment. More specifically, this amendment endangers the delivery of crucial humanitarian aid. Our country was in a different position when President Barack Obama entered the United States into a 10-year Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) in 2016. With the expiration of this MOU imminent, I believe change to our Middle East policy must happen to ensure the safety and security of both Israelis and Palestinians. These changes cannot come from a disgruntled Republican Member’s amendment that aims to divide Democrats and only allows for ten minutes of debate on the House Floor. For these reasons, I voted ‘no’ on this amendment, and will continue working with my colleagues to address the needs of both the Israeli and Palestinian people.”   ### Media Press Releases Back to top button

Congresswoman Luz Rivas Introduces Bill to Expand Access to Undergraduate Research STEM Programs | Representative Luz Rivas Skip to main content Congresswoman Luz Rivas Introduces Bill to Expand Access to Undergraduate Research STEM Programs August 27, 2026 Press Release LOS ANGELES – Congresswoman Luz Rivas (CA-29), co-chair of the STEM Education Caucus, introduced the National Science Foundation’s (NSF) Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU) Act of 2026. This bill reauthorizes and modernizes the NSF REU program that has strengthened undergraduate STEM research pathways since 2010. “Every college student, regardless of their background, deserves the opportunity to engage in STEM research, gain new experiences in the lab, and understand what a potential STEM career could be,” said Congresswoman Rivas. “Opportunities for STEM education experiences should not be limited because of where students go to school. My NSF REU Act expands access to undergraduate research experiences and opportunities to students at minority-serving institutions, community colleges, emerging research institutions, and rural-serving institutions. By strengthening learning opportunities for all students, we can develop a more inclusive and robust STEM workforce that will keep the United States a leader in innovation and technology.”  Background:  The National Science Foundation’s (NSF) Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU) Act of 2026 strengthens pathways into STEM careers by prioritizing first-time research participants and students from underrepresented and underserved backgrounds.
